PullRequest.Title: automations: feat: backport templates and target selection to 1.137
PullRequest.Body:
## Cherry-pick

Cherry-picks #334836 into `release/1.137`.

- Source commit: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b6d68fbe0a37b57967e1efa6bf19c24de9fa39b5
- One signed cherry-pick commit with `-x` provenance.
- Applied without conflicts or manual adaptations; the stable patch ID matches the source commit exactly.
- The provider-owned session-template prerequisite is already in this release through #334831.

## What this brings to 1.137

- **Starter automation templates:** editable issue-triage, pull-request-review, dependency-audit, and release-notes suggestions. Selecting a template opens the normal dialog; it does not create or schedule an automation.
- **Explicit targets:** new automations no longer silently inherit a recent GitHub workspace and appear locked to Cloud. Users choose a workspace or **No workspace** first. Single-agent targets explain the restriction and offer **Choose Workspace**; saved edit/duplicate targets and opaque provider configuration remain preserved.
- **Honest catalogue state:** distinguish `loading`, `ready`, `unavailable`, and `error` across stores, UI, accessible content, and `listAutomations`. Known automations and usable local targets remain available when a remote provider is offline. Only `ready` may claim that an empty catalogue means no automations.
- **Migration and focus safeguards:** retain visibility of unreadable legacy sources, recheck readability across migration boundaries, keep full-text template hovers, and preserve focus without stealing it after delayed updates.

Provider ownership, workspace trust, managed policy, and existing AI feature gating are unchanged. There are no dependency or persistence-schema changes.

## Release validation

- [x] **400 targeted Electron tests passed:** automation storage, providers, tools, Agent Host stores, cards view, dialog, and workspace/agent pickers.
- [x] Client type checking passed.
- [x] Targeted ESLint passed for the workspace-picker files auto-merged against release-specific code.
- [x] Stable patch equivalence, signed commit, clean worktree, and whitespace checks verified.

The source PR also passed its full GitHub CI and completed Copilot review without findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Automations view and react to provider catalogue or automation changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view reads the aggregate catalogue state and automation array, reconciles persistent cards, toggles one state container, and lazily renders four starter templates when the effective catalogue is empty. This work is on the view-update critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Maintain the Agent Host automation catalogue subscription used to project automation definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing subscription per instantiated Agent Host automation store; catalogue-state reads reuse that subscription and add no per-automation IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The store already acquired and consumed the same catalogue subscription to build its automations projection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial snapshot availability controls the loading state, but the diff does not add another IPC request or await to rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendering scales linearly with the number of available automations, as before; aggregate state scans the small provider-store set, and the template section is fixed at four cards.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates are synchronous and per-store; reconnect transitions are wrapped in transactions so consumers see one coherent emission. There is no new concurrent fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent automation cards are reused by ID, empty/template DOM is rendered once, and derived catalogue state recomputes only when provider registration or a participating store state changes. No new cache key or unbounded cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the view autorun, persistent-card map, one-time render flags, and provider-state derived observable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and automation counts vary, but the changed work is constant per state transition or shares the existing O(automations) reconciliation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added status/template UI is bounded, reuses persistent nodes, and catalogue observation does not create additional IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new automation dialog, select a target, and create from a starter template
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the dialog constructs its existing chat input and pickers plus a small target hint; target changes synchronously recompute available session types. A template click opens the normal dialog, and persistence occurs only after explicit confirmation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the confirmed automation through the existing automation service/store path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one create operation per confirmed dialog submission; selecting a template does not itself create or schedule an automation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior Create Automation action used the same dialog and createAutomation persistence path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing create operation remains on the submit critical path; the template only supplies initial scalar values.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session-type guidance scans providers/session types in memory on target/type events; realistic cardinality is the configured provider/type set, and four fixed templates are available.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dialog creation and automation creation are awaited serially, preserving the existing single user-action flow; no speculative or parallel creates are launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session picker already resolves the same provider/type lists; the new hint performs an additional in-memory lookup on relevant events but introduces no remote cache or repeated boundary lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from getSessionTypesForFolder being a synchronous provider iteration and from the explicit click/await create path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count can vary, but these arrays are expected to be small and the added scan occurs only while this dialog is open and target metadata changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: added work is bounded in-memory UI computation, and no new network, IPC, or filesystem call is triggered by template selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect, disconnect, or migrate an Agent Host automation catalogue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connection capability changes select the current store atomically. Migration still enumerates legacy definitions, performs its pre-existing per-definition migration, waits for the authoritative catalogue, dispatches completion, and drains pending imports; new readability checks are synchronous guards.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to the Agent Host automation catalogue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retained subscription per connected provider store, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The constructor already acquired this subscription for automation and run projections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial snapshot remains required for authoritative readiness and migration completion; catalogueState only observes the existing subscription.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Migrate legacy automation definitions and dispatch migration completion to the Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing migration work scales with the number of discovered legacy automations, followed by one completion dispatch; added checks do not increase boundary-call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Per-definition migration, catalogue waits, completion dispatch, and pending-import drain were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Migration waits for the same acknowledgements as before; the diff adds constant-time readability validation before/after waits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Boundary work scales with legacy automation count exactly as before. Aggregate state computation scales with current provider count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider migration remains sequenced and reconnect retries remain timer-controlled; state/store replacement is now transaction-coalesced rather than emitted separately.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current store and existing catalogue subscription are replaced and disposed through the established connection binding; no retained historical stores or catalogue keys are added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the constructor, migration loop, reconnect transactions, and tests covering single emissions and disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Migration population and IPC latency vary, but changed lines add only local state checks and atomic notifications.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff does not add migration IPC, increase fan-out, or weaken cleanup; it coalesces reconnect state changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll or move focus inside a custom view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native scroll events synchronize the DomScrollableElement model, while focus-induced browser scrolling is synchronized on the next animation frame.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost grows with native scroll event frequency, not item count. Each event reads one scrollTop and updates the existing scroll model; same-position updates are handled by the scroll model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scroll handling is synchronous O(1); focus synchronization keeps only the latest scheduled animation-frame callback via MutableDisposable.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The scheduled callback and listeners are disposed with the view node.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the event path and lifecycle; no evidence of an expensive layout boundary or feedback loop was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native scroll frequency depends on input device and content, but the operation matches established DomScrollableElement synchronization patterns elsewhere in the repository and does not establish forced layout or repeated DOM reconstruction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added synchronization is bounded and the focus callback is frame-scheduled and replaceable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke listAutomations or open the Automations accessible view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool serializes the currently available automation list with one added scalar state; the accessible view formats available automations/runs and appends four fixed templates when empty.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The tool remains O(number of automations) serialization; accessible content remains O(automations + visible runs), plus four constant template entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both paths are synchronous, user-invoked projections with no spawned work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both read current observables directly and retain no result cache or history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct map/JSON.stringify and line-building implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large automation/run collections increase existing string construction, but the diff adds only a scalar field and a fixed four-item section.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: serialization/allocation growth is unchanged asymptotically and the added output is constant-sized.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 25 changed files and relevant surrounding call paths. Checked UI hot paths, startup/service instantiation, provider catalogue lifecycle, migration IPC, persistence, scrolling, serialization, caching, concurrency, and cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found.
